- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- Model consistently overpredicts prices in the first 5–7 days of the 30d horizon, especially after recent spikes; apply a downward bias to early forecast points.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overreacts and forecasts continued ascent; cap forecast growth to 2–3% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts: if model is above 78–80 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) correlates with forecast divergence; when sentiment shifts sharply, reduce forecast confidence and apply smoothing (e.g., 3-day moving average) to avoid erratic predictions.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.2–0.4), model tends to err on the high side; use 1–2% downward adjustment to align with true mean.
